summary.intent: Unlock TurboQuant KV cache compression on a Framework Desktop with Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151), picking up from a prior session that had done BIOS changes and schema/oracle code but not the runtime integration.
summary.outcome: No TurboQuant dispatch was achieved this session, but the actual state of all prior work was fully mapped: 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 is already installed as an egg, the cohezion schema + PyTorch oracle exist, and the real blocker is a PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151 (not kernel/firmware/ROCm version). A smoke test was proposed but not yet run.

repo: 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 is installed at research/turboquant/ and importable from cohezion/.venv — CUDA-benchmarked (RTX 5090), not yet validated on AMD gfx1151

vLLM 0.19.0 in cohezion/.venv is broken: torch 2.5.1+rocm6.2 lacks torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass required by vLLM 0.19.0, and vLLM does not contain TurboQuant (no tbq/turbo flag exists in the package)
llama.cpp master is pre-built with HIP at ~/src/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server but is on master branch — no TurboQuant PR pulled
The fleet's only loaded model is DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B on port 13306 (NPU/FLM); other fleet ports are placeholder daemons with no model loaded
session 94 (2026-04-16) established that PyTorch ROCm wheels have a known upstream ISA gap for gfx1151 — HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1 is the correct override (not 11.5.0 as in some Gemini PDFs)
EmailNotifier class is imported by 5+ scripts but has no class definition in tracked code — orphaned import pattern
11+ near-duplicate send_*.py scripts exist; should be consolidated into one scripts/send_handoff.py
local_environment_quirks.md is the authoritative record of session-94 findings and distilled TURBOQUANT_UNLOCK_REPORT.md content

code.finding: Complete 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 package with Triton kernels, vLLM attention backend plugin, benchmarks, and proof tests. Installed as egg. Integration is via VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND registration, not a CLI flag like --kv-cache-dtype tbq4.
Returns silently (return) when GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD is missing — silent-failure anti-pattern. Should raise SystemExit(2) instead.
Contains known-good llama.cpp launch flags: -fa 1 -ngl 99 and HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1. Should be consulted before launching llama-server manually.
PyTorch oracle (178 lines) for correctness gating. Separate from the 0xSero Triton kernels — used to validate dispatch output matches paper tolerances.
Read-only probe using sysfs mem_info_vram_total and lspci -vv LnkSta proxies. Cannot detect AI Max Performance BIOS toggle (only visible via thermal/frequency telemetry under load).

workflow: Gmail MCP create_draft bypasses GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD entirely and is safer for human-in-the-loop handoffs — MCP intentionally exposes create_draft but not send, requiring human review before delivery
llama.cpp default -fit on hangs at 99% CPU for 2+ minutes on large models; use -fit off to bypass
On Strix Halo UMA APU, model buffers land in GTT (shared system memory), not VRAM — rocm-smi VRAM Used stays flat while GTT Used grows; this is expected behavior
rocm-smi reports full 64 GB while HSA per-process ceiling shows ~31 GB — the discrepancy is HSA user-segment allocation ceiling, not a VRAM loss; 64 GB is accessible
kernel.ubuntu.com mainline v6.18.4 build failed (directory exists, no .debs); use v6.18.23 (latest longterm, built 2026-04-18) instead
Adding a third-party PPA (cappelikan/ppa) is a persistent system change that deserves explicit consent separate from 'upgrade kernel' — direct .deb from kernel.ubuntu.com is safer and auditable
Bitwarden CLI pointed at self-hosted server (mike-poweredge-t30.tail54eb71.ts.net:8222) which may not be reachable from all network contexts
Before cloning external forks or installing new software, audit local disk for existing installs — in this case, turboquant was already installed and llama.cpp was already built
